record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given an undirected graph G and positive integers k and d, can the vertex set V(G) be partitioned into disjoint subsets V1, ..., Vm such that each part Vi has size at most k and at most d edges have exactly one endpoint in Vi?

evidence.quote:
Minimum Degree Graph Partition FPT
Instance: An undirected graphG
Parameter: Positive integersk and d
Question: Can V(G) be partitioned into disjoint subsetsV1,...,V m so
that for 1≤i ≤m, |Vi|≤ k and at mostd edges have exactly one endpoint
in Vi?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple undirected graph, and let k and d be positive integers. Decide whether there exists a partition of V into pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets V_1, V_2, …, V_m (for some m ≥ 1) such that, for every i ∈ {1, …, m}:

(i) |V_i| ≤ k, and
(ii) the number of edges of G having exactly one endpoint in V_i is at most d (equivalently, each part V_i has at most d boundary edges in G).

The question is whether this decision problem is fixed-parameter tractable when jointly parameterized by k and d; that is, whether it admits an algorithm running in time f(k, d) · |V(G)|^{O(1)} for some computable function f.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is reported as fixed-parameter tractable: the 2011 result that graph immersion testing is FPT (Grohe–Kawarabayashi–Marx–Wollan) implies that Minimum Degree Graph Partition is FPT when parameterized by (k, d), since a graph admits such a partition iff it does not contain a certain finite family of immersion-obstructions depending only on k and d.

status_evidence.title: FPT suspects and tough customers: Open problems of Downey and Fellows
status_evidence.snippet: The result from 2011 that immersion testing is FPT immediately implies that Minimum Degree Graph Partition is FPT.
status_evidence.claim: Minimum Degree Graph Partition is FPT, as a consequence of FPT immersion testing.
